claims.statement: dcode detects --acp in raw argv to skip Textual UI dependency checks, lazily imports ACP dependencies, and prints an install hint before exiting 1 if acp or deepagents-acp are missing.

In dcode ACP mode, the resolved approval mode—not raw flags—governs the YOLO acknowledgement and Auto classifier checks; YOLO requires a prior interactive-TUI acknowledgement, --auto-classifier-model requires Auto mode, and --no-mcp and --mcp-config are mutually exclusive.

AgentServerACP accepts either a compiled graph or an AgentSessionContext factory; only factories may be configured with modes or models, and supplying those selectors for a compiled graph raises ValueError.

During initialization and session creation, the adapter advertises image input and optionally session loading, creates a unique session ID, retains cwd and supplied ACP MCP descriptors, initializes selectors, and persists session metadata when durable loading is enabled.

Session configuration selectors validate string values and recognised choices, then reset the session graph; a factory receives the resulting cwd, mode, and model in AgentSessionContext while the LangGraph thread ID stays equal to the ACP session ID.

For an ACP prompt, the adapter streams the graph in messages and updates with subgraphs enabled, exposes only top-level assistant content and plaintext reasoning while suppressing messages tagged as local context, maps todos to plans, and delays tool starts until accumulated arguments parse as JSON.

The adapter rejects free-form LangGraph interrupts because ACP can only display fixed permission choices; it obtains decisions for HumanInTheLoopMiddleware-style action requests and resumes the graph, treating a cancelled permission request as rejection.

Always-allow permission decisions are stored only in adapter memory per ACP session; execute reuse requires an exact canonical serialization of the full tool arguments paired with the current cwd, mode, and model, while non-execute tools are allowlisted by name.

Durable session loading requires a checkpointed ACP-marked graph thread with the original cwd, restores persisted supported mode/model selections, and replays conversation and tool history through session updates while excluding messages tagged as local context.

The generic adapter retains ACP MCP descriptors but does not expose them through AgentSessionContext or convert them into graph tools; dcode instead resolves MCP tools from its configuration, trust context, and plugin configurations before constructing session graphs and cleans up its MCP manager on exit.

Dcode ACP startup resolves the initial model and available model selectors, builds web/MCP/subagent tools, opens dcode's checkpointer, and supplies a per-session graph factory with session cwd and selected model to an ownership-aware AgentServerACP configured for session loading.

In dcode Auto ACP mode, a specialized AgentServerACP wraps graphs to write trusted Auto approval state, attach prompt metadata, and pass CLIContextSchema with Auto approval settings for each graph stream.
The --acp CLI option runs an ACP server over stdio instead of launching dcode's Textual UI; the normal remote client lazily creates a LangGraph RemoteGraph.

ACP input conversion accepts text, inline images, resource links, and embedded resources; resource-link paths are made relative to the session root, embedded blobs become data URIs, and input audio is not supported.

The adapter checks a shared cancellation flag before and during graph streaming, returns a cancelled prompt response when it is set, and waits for the stream iterator to close before reading interrupt state to avoid stale persistent-checkpoint snapshots.
Dcode reports missing MCP configuration files and MCP tool-loading failures to stderr and returns exit code 1 before opening its ACP server.
If a prompted graph lacks a checkpointer, the adapter assigns MemorySaver for that turn, whereas session persistence and loading explicitly require a graph compiled with a checkpointer.

dcode's ACP wrapper acquires a local lease before session graph configuration, attaches the lease token to the graph configuration, releases it when the adapter forgets the session or the runner exits, and rejects a session thread that is already open elsewhere.
The dcode ownership-fenced SQLite saver validates the configuration lease token before checkpoint writes, so stale or released ACP clients cannot mutate a thread after ownership changes.
The ACP launcher tests verify that a second ownership-aware server cannot load a thread held by the first, and that writes using the first server's old configuration fail after ownership transfers.

dcode 0.2.8 requires Python 3.14, while its package declares deepagents-acp version 0.0.13 or later as a dependency, so dcode ACP deployments follow dcode's stricter Python requirement rather than deepagents-acp's standalone Python 3.11 floor.
The adapter suppresses messages tagged `lc_source="local_context"` during live projection and durable replay, keeping local environment context out of the ACP editor transcript.

The ownership-fenced SQLite saver acquires a thread lease before deletion and holds the writer guard through the deletion, refusing to delete a thread open elsewhere and releasing its temporary lease afterward.
deepagents-acp 0.0.13 fixes reusable shell authorization to exact commands and preserves local-context prompts across compaction.

deepagents-acp 0.0.13 is an alpha package requiring Python 3.11 or later, deepagents, agent-client-protocol>=0.10.1, and python-dotenv>=1.2.2; its README presents AgentServerACP as the custom graph adapter and dcode --acp as the ready-made coding-agent alternative.
Before ACP dispatch, dcode applies its managed-configuration health gate; an unenforceable managed policy is written to stderr and terminates the process with exit status 78.
